title: Money transfer service

public.intro: An assistant wrote this transfer method for a banking feature. It compiles and the happy-path test passes. Click every line that contains a real defect.

bugs.title: Not atomic, no input validation
bugs.explanation: No @Transactional, so a crash between the two saves creates or destroys money. The method also accepts amountCents ≤ 0 (a negative amount reverses the transfer) and fromId == toId.

bugs.title: Check-then-act race
bugs.explanation: Two concurrent transfers can both pass the balance check, then both debit, overdrawing the account. Use a single conditional UPDATE (balance = balance - ? WHERE balance >= ?), a row lock (SELECT … FOR UPDATE), or optimistic versioning.

explanation: Money code needs atomicity, protection against concurrent updates, and input validation. Plausible-looking generated code usually covers the happy path only.

title: Find users by name

public.intro: Generated data-access code. Click every line that contains a real defect.

bugs.title: SQL injection
bugs.explanation: User input is concatenated into SQL. A name like ' OR '1'='1 returns every user. Use a PreparedStatement with a ? parameter.

bugs.title: Resource leak
bugs.explanation: Connection, Statement and ResultSet are never closed. Under load this exhausts the connection pool. Use try-with-resources.

explanation: These are two of the oldest defects in data-access code, and they still appear in generated code all the time.

title: Binary search

public.intro: An assistant wrote this search for a sorted int array. Click every line that contains a real defect.

bugs.title: Bounds mismatch
bugs.explanation: hi starts at a.length but the loop uses lo <= hi, so mid can equal a.length and throw ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException. Use hi = a.length - 1 with lo <= hi (or hi = a.length with lo < hi).

bugs.title: Infinite loop
bugs.explanation: lo = mid doesn't make progress when lo == mid (e.g. two elements left). It must be lo = mid + 1.

bugs.title: Overflow
bugs.explanation: (lo + hi) can overflow int for very large arrays. Use lo + (hi - lo) / 2 or (lo + hi) >>> 1.

explanation: Binary search is famously easy to get subtly wrong. Check that the invariant, the loop condition and the update rules agree with each other.

title: In-memory rate limiter

public.intro: A rate limiter singleton called from many request threads at once. Click every line that contains a real defect.

bugs.title: Not thread-safe
bugs.explanation: HashMap under concurrent writes can lose updates and corrupt its internal structure. Use ConcurrentHashMap.

bugs.title: Check-then-act race
bugs.explanation: Even with ConcurrentHashMap, get → compare → put isn't atomic, so concurrent requests exceed the limit. Use counts.merge(key, 1, Integer::sum) or compute(), and compare the returned value.

explanation: A concurrent collection makes single operations safe, not sequences of them. That distinction is one of the most valuable things to check in reviews.

title: Money value object

public.intro: A value object used as a key in HashMap and HashSet. Click every line that contains a real defect.

bugs.title: String compared with ==
bugs.explanation: == compares references. Two equal currency strings built at runtime (e.g. parsed from JSON) aren't ==. Use currency.equals(m.currency) or Objects.equals.

bugs.title: equals without hashCode
bugs.explanation: Overriding equals without hashCode breaks the contract: equal Money values land in different hash buckets, so HashSet and HashMap lookups fail. A record would generate both.

explanation: Value objects are a great fit for Java records, which get equals, hashCode and toString right automatically.

title: "Robust" payment retry

public.intro: An assistant was asked to make payment calls 'robust'. Click every line that contains a real defect.

bugs.title: Unbounded retries
bugs.explanation: attempt is counted but never checked. A persistent failure blocks the thread forever. Cap the number of attempts and surface the failure.

bugs.title: Retrying a non-idempotent charge
bugs.explanation: A timeout may mean the charge succeeded. Retrying without a stable idempotency key causes double charges.

bugs.title: Retries everything
bugs.explanation: Catching Exception also retries permanent errors such as a declined card or validation failure (4xx). Retry only transient failures.

bugs.title: Swallowed interrupt
bugs.explanation: Ignoring InterruptedException makes shutdown hang. Restore the flag with Thread.currentThread().interrupt() and stop.

bugs.title: No backoff or jitter
bugs.explanation: A fixed 1 s sleep in every client hammers a struggling provider in lockstep. Use exponential backoff with jitter.

explanation: 'Robust' code that retries blindly is often the cause of the outage. Good retry logic is bounded, selective, idempotent, interruptible, and backs off with jitter.
